title: 32.1 A 180MHz 45.3%-Peak-Efficiency Isolated Converter Using Q-Downsize Class-D Power Amplifier with Inherent Shoot-Through Current Blocking and High Tolerance for Efficiency Despite Frequency Misalignments
problem: Isolated DC-DC converters suffer from high electromagnetic interference (EMI) due to common-mode (CM) current across the isolation barrier; suppressing CM voltage variation requires fully symmetrical transmitter (TX) topologies but introduces complexity.
motivation: Industrial applications in harsh environments require low-EMI isolated converters with high efficiency and robustness to circuit parameter variations (frequency misalignment).
method: The design uses a simplified switching amplifier (Class-D power amplifier with Q-downsize technique) that naturally prevents shoot-through current—the dangerous short circuit when both transistors conduct simultaneously—which eliminates the need for artificial delays that normally reduce efficiency. The transmitter is built with perfectly symmetrical circuits on both sides of the isolation barrier, and the coils wind in opposite directions so their magnetic fields cancel each other; this symmetry automatically suppresses the electromagnetic interference that normally leaks across isolated converters. The circuit operates at 180MHz and achieves 45.3% peak efficiency, with stable performance even when the switching frequency varies from its target.
key_novelty: A simplified Class-D switching amplifier (the Q-downsize technique) that naturally blocks shoot-through current surges without needing efficiency-stealing delays, while maintaining stable performance despite frequency variations.
contributions: Reduced EMI via symmetrical topology and coil cancellation
primary_theme: High-efficiency isolated converter with robustness to misalignment
